summary:
Space Arcade is a multi-page website that brings four browser games together in one place. Each game has its own page, and each page pairs the game with a short, factual section about the real space topic that inspired it. Visitors play the game first, then learn something about space science.

The games are Stickman Archer vs Aliens, Monster Run, Power Rover and Space Game. They connect to four topics: the search for alien life, the moons of the solar system, Mars rovers, and the solar system with the International Space Station. The information is written in our own words from NASA and Wikipedia-style space facts.
 It works on both phones and computers, and its colors switch between light and dark mode to match the device. The project shows that games can make science topics more engaging and easier to remember.
details:
1. OBJECTIVES -

Bring several independent games together in one easy-to-use website. - Give every game an educational section based on real space facts. - Make the site simple to navigate on phones and computers. - Encourage curiosity about space science.

2. PAGES AND GAMES-

Home Page Welcomes visitors and shows a card for each game. Clicking a card opens that game's page. Stickman Archer vs Aliens An aim-and-shoot game against aliens. Topic: The search for life beyond Earth. Covers astrobiology, exoplanets (thousands confirmed since 1995), the habitable zone, SETI, NASA's Kepler telescope, the Drake equation (1961), and how the James Webb Space Telescope studies distant planet atmospheres. Monster Run A lane-running game on an alien moon where the player dodges obstacles, collects sapphires and escapes a monster. Topic: Moons of the solar system. Covers the Moon (about 384,400 km from Earth, one sixth of Earth's gravity, Apollo 11 in 1969), Europa and its hidden ocean (Europa Clipper, launched 2024), Enceladus and its water plumes, Titan and its methane lakes (Dragonfly rotorcraft), and the Artemis program. Power Rover A rover driving game with fuel, rough terrain and sample collecting. Topic: Rovers on Mars. Covers Sojourner (1997), Spirit and Opportunity (2004), Curiosity (2012), Perseverance (2021) and the helicopter Ingenuity. Also covers the Martian day (sol) of about 24 hours 37 minutes and Mars gravity of roughly 38 percent of Earth's. Space Game A space-themed game. Topic: The solar system and the International Space Station. Covers the eight planets, the Sun holding about 99.8 percent of the system's mass, and the ISS orbiting at about 400 km and 28,000 km/h, with around 16 sunrises a day and continuous human presence since November 2000.

3. FEATURES -

Top menu bar that stays visible while scrolling, with KRYOS in capital letters at the top right. - A Play button on each game page that opens the game in a new tab. - Fact cards and a short explanation under each game. - Responsive layout for phone and desktop. - Automatic light and dark mode.

4. TECHNOLOGY -

The whole site is one HTML file using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no outside libraries. - Page switching uses link anchors such as #rover, so no page reloads are needed. - The four games are separate projects hosted on Netlify and linked from the site.

5. CHALLENGE AND SOLUTION -

The plan was to embed each game inside its page. The hosting used for publishing blocked this and showed a "This content is blocked" message. To fix it, each game page now has a Play button that opens the game in a new tab, with the info section placed right below it. A second version with the games embedded is also available for hosting on a service such as Netlify, where it works if the game sites allow embedding.

6. LEARNING OUTCOMES -

Visitors can learn: - What exoplanets are and how scientists search for life beyond Earth. - Why icy moons are important targets for exploration. - How Mars rovers work and what they have found. - The basic structure of the solar system and the role of the ISS.

7. FUTURE IMPROVEMENTS -

Add screenshots for each game. - Add quiz questions after each info section. - Add more games and space topics. - Add a score tracker or leaderboard. 8. CONCLUSION Space Arcade connects simple browser games to real space science, giving players a reason to read about the science after playing. It is lightweight, works on any device, and can grow with more games and topics.
